q: Walk me through the case lifecycle in Service Cloud from start to finish.
alt: Explain the end to end case lifecycle
what happens to a case from creation to closure
case management process in service cloud step by step
How does a support ticket flow through Salesforce?
a: I'd describe it as six stages, and I design each one deliberately. A case gets created, routed, worked under an SLA, solved with knowledge, closed, and then we ask for feedback. Take a laptop seller. A customer emails support about a dead battery, so Email-to-Case creates a case with Origin Email, links it to the contact by the sender address, and an auto-response rule sends a 'we got it' email with the case number. Assignment rules or Omni-Channel put it in the Hardware queue and push it to an available agent. Because the account has a Gold entitlement, the case gets a First Response milestone, and milestone warnings or escalation rules alert the manager if it sits too long. The agent finds a Knowledge article, replies from the case feed using a macro, and closes the case with a resolution. A flow then sends a CSAT survey. If the customer replies later, email threading attaches the reply to the same case.
points: Create: Email, Web, phone, chat or messaging, portal
Route: assignment rules, queues, Omni-Channel
SLA: entitlements, milestones, escalation rules
Solve: Knowledge, macros, quick text
Close and measure: closed status, resolution, survey

q: What are the different ways a case can be created in Service Cloud?
alt: What are the case origin channels?
how do cases come into salesforce
Case creation channels in Service Cloud
From where can customers raise a case?
a: Cases can come in from almost every channel, and my rule is that each one sets the Case Origin so you can report on it. Email-to-Case turns emails sent to a support address into cases. Web-to-Case is a simple HTML form on the website. For phone, the agent creates the case from the softphone in the console through Open CTI or Service Cloud Voice. Chat and messaging, like Enhanced Chat, WhatsApp or SMS, create Messaging Sessions that the agent or a flow links to a case. On an Experience Cloud help portal, logged-in customers create cases themselves. Cases can also come from an Agentforce service agent action or from another system through the API. Example: a clinic takes appointment issues by phone, billing questions by email and requests from patients on the portal, and all of them land in the same Case object, so one queue and one report can cover them.
points: Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case
Phone via Open CTI or Service Cloud Voice
Enhanced Chat and messaging apps
Experience Cloud portal, AI agent, API
Case Origin field tracks the channel

q: Once a case is created, how does it reach the right agent?
alt: How are cases assigned to agents?
case routing in service cloud explained
pull vs push model for cases
Who decides which agent gets a new case?
a: It reaches the agent either by pull or by push, and for most teams I'd recommend push. With pull, case assignment rules set the owner to a queue or a user based on criteria, and agents pick work from the queue list view. With push, Omni-Channel takes cases from a queue, or uses skills, and sends each one to an available agent who has free capacity, so nobody picks and chooses. Example: an electronics retailer gets a case with Type Refund. The assignment rule sends it to the Billing queue. That queue is linked to an Omni-Channel routing configuration, so the case is pushed to the billing agent who is online and has the least work. If it needs a Spanish speaker, skills-based routing adds a Spanish skill. Two things I make sure the team knows: only one case assignment rule can be active, its entries are checked in order and the first match wins, and that Omni-Channel is what balances the load.
points: Assignment rules set owner to user or queue
Only one active assignment rule; first matching entry wins
Omni-Channel pushes work based on availability and capacity
Skills-based routing for language or product

q: How does the right entitlement get onto a case, and what happens to milestones as the case moves along?
alt: How do you auto populate entitlement on a case?
when does the SLA clock start on a case
entitlement process flow during case lifecycle
How are case milestones created and completed?
a: The entitlement is what starts the SLA clock, so it has to be on the case early, ideally right at creation. Agents can pick it in the Entitlement lookup, but on my projects I set it with a before-save flow, because agents forget: find the active entitlement for the case's account, or for the asset if SLAs are per product, and fill EntitlementId. Once that's set, the entitlement process checks the case and creates Case Milestone records, like First Response and Resolution, each with a target date worked out from business hours. As the case moves, a milestone is completed when its completion date is set, it shows as violated if the target passes first, and the process ends when the case meets its exit criteria, usually closed. Example: a manufacturer's Platinum customer logs a case, the flow sets the Platinum entitlement, and a one-hour First Response milestone appears in the milestone tracker on the case.
points: Entitlement must be on the case for milestones to start
Before-save flow looks up active entitlement by account or asset
Case Milestone records hold target and completion dates
Milestones can be completed, violated or stopped

q: Where does Knowledge fit into the case lifecycle?
alt: How do agents use knowledge articles on cases?
knowledge and case deflection
attach article to case salesforce
What is KCS in Service Cloud?
a: Knowledge shows up at three points: before a case exists, while the agent works it, and after it's solved. Before, customers search articles on the help portal, or an Agentforce service agent answers from them, which stops simple cases from being created at all. During, the Knowledge component on the case suggests articles based on the subject, and the agent can attach one or insert it into the email reply. After, if the agent solved something new, they create or flag an article from the case so the next person doesn't start from zero, which is the idea behind KCS. Example: a router company gets a case saying Wi-Fi drops every hour. The agent sees the article 'Update firmware to fix Wi-Fi drops', attaches it, sends the steps and closes the case. Because the article is attached, you can later report on which articles solve the most cases. On a team I'd make flagging new articles part of how agents close cases, not an extra task.
points: Before: self-service and AI agent deflection
During: suggested articles, attach or insert into reply
After: create articles from solved cases (KCS)
Attached articles give reporting on usefulness

q: What should happen when a case is closed?
alt: How do you design case closure?
case close process best practices
what happens at case closure in salesforce
Closed statuses and resolution fields
a: Closing should capture how the case was solved and kick off the follow-up, not just flip the status. I set up a few closed status values, like Closed - Resolved, Closed - Duplicate and Closed - No Response, which all set IsClosed to true so reports and SLAs treat them as done. The close action or path asks for fields like Resolution and Root Cause, usually backed by a validation rule. Milestones on the case complete or the entitlement process exits, and a flow sends the CSAT survey and maybe a closing email. Example: an appliance company closes a case about a faulty fridge door. The agent picks Closed - Resolved, writes 'Replaced hinge under warranty', and the survey goes to the customer. One thing I get the business to decide up front is reopening: does a reply to a closed case reopen it, or create a new case linked to the old one?
points: Use multiple closed status values with IsClosed true
Require Resolution and Root Cause on close
Close milestones and trigger the survey
Decide the reopen policy early

q: How would you collect customer satisfaction feedback after a case is closed?
alt: How do you send a CSAT survey on case close?
salesforce surveys after case closure
automate survey invitation when case closes
How do you measure CSAT in Service Cloud?
a: I'd use Salesforce Surveys with a record-triggered flow on Case. First I enable Surveys, build a short CSAT survey with one rating question and an optional comment, and activate it. Then a record-triggered flow runs when Status changes to Closed and uses the Send Surveys action, with the case as the survey subject, the case contact as the recipient, a unique link so each response maps back, and an expiry of about a week. For external customers the survey is served through an Experience Cloud site, so the guest user needs access to surveys, invitations and responses. Example: a telecom closes a lot of cases every day, so I'd add entry conditions to skip Closed - Duplicate and spam cases, and not survey the same contact more than once a week. Responses link back to the case, so I can report CSAT by agent, queue and case reason. I'd agree those rules with the support manager first, because survey fatigue hurts response rates.
points: Salesforce Surveys plus record-triggered flow on close
Send Surveys action with case as subject
Experience Cloud site and guest access for external recipients
Filter out duplicates and over-surveying

q: Walk me through the lifecycle of a customer chat in Enhanced Chat.
alt: How does a web chat flow from start to end in Salesforce?
enhanced chat conversation lifecycle
What happens when a customer starts a chat on the website?
chat to case flow with agentforce and omni channel
a: A chat starts on the website, gets routed, is often handled by AI first, then a human if needed, and ends linked to a case. Say a shoe store has Enhanced Chat (formerly Messaging for In-App and Web) on its site. The customer opens the chat and fills the pre-chat form with name and order number. That creates a Messaging Session, and an Omni-Channel flow decides where it goes, usually an Agentforce service agent first. The AI agent answers 'where is my order' using a flow action. When the customer asks about a refund it can't handle, it transfers to the Returns queue with context, and Omni-Channel pushes the conversation to an agent with capacity. The agent sees the full transcript, creates or links a case for the refund, and ends the conversation. Because it's asynchronous, the customer can leave and come back to the same thread later. Reporting uses Messaging Session and AgentWork. When I plan a rollout like this, I agree the AI-to-human handoff rules with the support manager before anything goes live.
points: Pre-chat form, then Messaging Session is created
Omni-Channel flow routes to AI agent, queue or rep
Handoff to a human with context
Asynchronous: customer can return to the same conversation
Link or create a case for follow-up

q: What happens to a phone call in Service Cloud Voice, from the first ring to wrap-up?
alt: Explain the call flow in Service Cloud Voice
voice call lifecycle in salesforce
how does an inbound call work with amazon connect and salesforce
What does the agent see when a call comes in?
a: In Service Cloud Voice, a call is a work item in the console and it creates a Voice Call record. Example for a bank: a customer calls, the telephony side, like Amazon Connect, plays the IVR and collects the account number. The call is routed to an available agent in the right queue, and the softphone in the console rings. When the agent answers, the console opens the matching contact, the Voice Call record shows, and real-time transcription appears as they talk. The agent creates or updates a case linked to the call, uses Knowledge or AI suggestions, and can transfer or bring in a supervisor. After hanging up, the agent finishes wrap-up, like notes and disposition. The recording and transcript stay with the Voice Call, so AI can summarize it and supervisors can review it later. When I explain it to stakeholders, the big win over a basic CTI softphone is that voice sits in the same routing and reporting as other channels.
points: Call creates a VoiceCall record
IVR on telephony side, routing to an agent
Screen pop of contact and live transcript
Case linked to the call, then wrap-up
Transcript enables AI summaries

q: How does a case raised on the Experience Cloud help portal move through its lifecycle?
alt: What happens when a customer logs a case in the community?
portal case lifecycle salesforce
customer creates case on experience site, then what
How do customers track their cases in a portal?
a: A portal case follows the same lifecycle as any other case; the difference is the customer creates and follows it themselves. Example: a software company's customer logs in to the help center and clicks Contact Support. As they type the subject, the site suggests Knowledge articles, which deflects some cases. If they still submit, a case is created with the contact and account taken from their user, and the assignment rule puts it in a queue. The customer sees it under My Cases, can add comments or files, and gets an email when the agent replies. The agent answers from the case feed and chooses whether each post is visible to the customer. When the case closes, the customer sees the new status and gets the survey. The setup pieces I review most carefully are sharing, so customers only see their own or their account's cases, and which fields and feed items are visible externally.
points: Article suggestions before submit
Contact and account set from the portal user
My Cases list, comments and files
External visibility on feed posts
Sharing sets or sharing rules control access

q: What case statuses would you set up for a support team, and why?
alt: How do you design case status values?
what are good case statuses in service cloud
case status best practices
Why have a Waiting on Customer status?
a: I keep statuses few and meaningful, so each one tells you who has the ball. A typical set is New, In Progress, Waiting on Customer, Waiting on Third Party, Escalated, and a few closed values like Closed - Resolved, Closed - Duplicate and Closed - No Response. Example: a printer company's agent asks the customer for a serial number and moves the case to Waiting on Customer. That status can stop the SLA milestone clock, start a seven-day auto-close timer, and keep the case out of the agent's backlog count. When the customer replies, a flow moves it back to In Progress. Different teams can have different status lists through support processes and record types. I avoid lots of near-duplicate statuses, because every status needs reports, automation and training around it, and agents start picking them randomly. So I review any new status request against that before agreeing to it.
points: Each status says who owns the next step
Waiting statuses can pause SLAs and start auto-close
Support processes give teams different status lists
Fewer statuses means cleaner reports

q: What are the main features of Service Cloud?
alt: Tell me the key features of Salesforce Service Cloud
what all comes in service cloud
service cloud capabilities overview
What can you do with Service Cloud?
a: Service Cloud is Salesforce's customer support product built around the Case object, and I group its features into four buckets. Channels: Email-to-Case, Web-to-Case, the Experience Cloud help portal, Enhanced Chat, messaging apps like WhatsApp and SMS, and phone through Service Cloud Voice or Open CTI. Routing and SLAs: assignment rules, queues, Omni-Channel, escalation rules, entitlements, milestones and service contracts. Agent productivity: the Service Console, macros, quick text, Knowledge, case teams and swarming in Slack. AI and insight: Agentforce service agents that talk to customers, assistive features like Case Classification, Service Replies and Work Summaries, and Omni Supervisor and dashboards for managers. Example: a travel company takes booking issues over WhatsApp, routes them through Omni-Channel by language, tracks a two-hour response SLA with milestones, and lets an AI agent answer baggage questions. Field Service is a separate product for on-site work that usually starts from a case. With a stakeholder, I'd pick the bucket that matches their biggest pain and start there.
points: Channels: email, web, portal, chat, messaging, voice
Routing and SLAs: Omni-Channel, entitlements, milestones
Productivity: console, macros, quick text, Knowledge
AI: Agentforce service agent and assistive features

q: What is the difference between tab-based and status-based capacity in Omni-Channel?
alt: Explain status based capacity model
tab based vs status based capacity omni channel
When is agent capacity released in Omni-Channel?
capacity model for cases that stay open for days
a: For long-running cases I'd usually pick status-based. Both decide when an agent's capacity is used and freed; the difference is what frees it. Tab-based is the default: a routed case uses capacity from the moment the agent accepts it until they close the console tab. Status-based ties capacity to a picklist field on the record, usually Case Status. In the service channel you map each value to In Progress, Completed or Paused, and only In Progress uses capacity. Example: an insurance claims team keeps cases open for days. With tab-based, an agent with five open tabs looks full even if they're waiting on documents. With status-based, moving a case to Waiting on Customer, mapped to Paused, frees capacity, so Omni-Channel sends them a new case. Status-based is meant for records like cases and leads, not for chat, messaging or voice. The risk I plan for: if agents forget to update the status, capacity stays locked, so I pair it with a report on cases sitting In Progress too long.
points: Tab-based (default): capacity freed when tab closes
Status-based: picklist values mapped to In Progress, Completed, Paused
Only In Progress consumes capacity
Status-based is for records like cases, not chat or voice

q: What is an Omni-Channel flow, and when would you use it instead of a plain routing configuration?
alt: Explain Omni-Channel Flow and the Route Work action
omni channel flow vs queue based routing configuration
How do you route messaging with a flow?
what is route work action in salesforce
a: An Omni-Channel flow is a special flow type that decides how a work item is routed, using the Route Work action, instead of relying only on a queue's routing configuration. A queue plus routing configuration is fine when everything in that queue goes to one group. I use an Omni-Channel flow when routing depends on data: look up the account tier, add skills like language and product, check whether agents are online with the Check Availability for Routing action, and then route to a queue, a specific agent, a set of skills, or an Agentforce agent. Example: for a telecom's chat, the flow reads the pre-chat Topic field, sees it's a business account, adds Business and Spanish skills, and if no agent with those skills is online, sends the chat to the AI agent first. Enhanced Chat and messaging channels are routed with these flows, so it's becoming the standard way to route. So for new work I'd default the team to flows and keep plain routing configurations for the simple queues.
points: Flow type that routes work with the Route Work action
Route to queue, agent, skills or AI agent
Check Availability for Routing before deciding
Standard for Enhanced Chat and messaging

q: What is Digital Engagement in Service Cloud?
alt: What does the Digital Engagement add-on include?
digital engagement license salesforce
How do customers message support on WhatsApp in Salesforce?
messaging channels add-on for service cloud
a: Digital Engagement is the Service Cloud add-on that gives you messaging channels beyond email and phone, handled from the same console. It covers Enhanced Chat on your website or app and messaging apps like SMS, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger and Apple Messages for Business, all routed through Omni-Channel. Each conversation is a Messaging Session linked to a messaging end user, so agents can see the history across channels. Example: a food delivery company lets customers text a number about late orders. The SMS lands in Salesforce, Omni-Channel routes it to an agent, the agent replies from the console, and links it to a case if it needs follow-up. A practical tip: if an admin creates a new messaging channel and doesn't see the Enhanced Chat option, it usually means the org doesn't have the Digital Engagement license yet. I'd confirm licensing with the client before promising any channel in a plan.
points: Add-on for chat and messaging channels
Enhanced Chat, SMS, WhatsApp, Messenger, Apple Messages
Conversations are Messaging Sessions routed by Omni-Channel
Missing Enhanced Chat option often means no license

q: What AI features does Service Cloud give to human support agents?
alt: Explain Einstein and Agentforce features for service reps
what is service replies and work summaries
AI features in service console
How does AI help agents in Service Cloud?
a: Besides the customer-facing Agentforce service agent, there's a set of assistive features for human reps. Case Classification predicts fields like Type, Reason or Priority from the subject and description, and Case Routing uses those predictions to send the case to the right queue. Article Recommendations suggests Knowledge articles on the case. Reply Recommendations suggests approved replies during chat and messaging, while Service Replies uses generative AI to draft a full reply that the rep edits before sending. Work Summaries drafts a summary, issue and resolution at the end of a conversation, and Knowledge Creation drafts an article from solved work. Agentforce Service Assistant can draft a step-by-step resolution plan on a case. Example: a phone company's agent opens a case about a cracked screen; the type is already predicted, a repair article is suggested, and after the chat the summary is filled in. The rep always reviews before anything goes out. That review step is the guardrail I'd hold the team to, especially early on.
points: Case Classification and Case Routing
Article Recommendations and Reply Recommendations
Service Replies and Work Summaries (generative)
Knowledge Creation and Service Assistant plans
Human reviews before sending

q: How does Einstein Case Classification work, and how would you roll it out?
alt: Explain case classification in Salesforce
einstein predicts case fields how
auto fill case reason using AI
How do you set up Case Classification?
a: Case Classification learns from your closed cases and predicts field values on new cases, like Case Reason, Type, Priority or Product, from the subject and description. You pick which fields to predict, it builds a model from historical cases, and then it can recommend values to the agent or fill them in automatically when it's confident. Example: an online store gets thousands of emails, and agents waste time setting the Reason. After training on past closed cases, the model learns that 'where is my parcel' means Reason equals Shipping. My rollout plan is to start with recommendations only, check accuracy per field, then switch to auto-fill for the fields that are reliable and use them in assignment rules or Omni-Channel routing. The catch is data quality: if agents picked random reasons in the past, the model learns random reasons, so I'd clean up the picklists and history first.
points: Predicts case fields from subject and description
Trained on historical closed cases
Recommend first, auto-fill when accurate
Clean picklist data before training

q: What is Swarming in Service Cloud?
alt: How does swarming with Slack work?
case swarming salesforce slack
What is Expert Finder in swarming?
swarm vs escalation in support
a: Swarming lets an agent pull experts into a Slack channel tied to a case, so a hard case gets solved together instead of being passed around through escalations. From the case, the agent clicks Begin Swarming, a Slack channel is created, usually named after the case number, and they describe the help they need. They can add specific people, or use Expert Finder, which looks at skills and Omni-Channel availability to suggest and invite the right expert. Example: a solar company's agent has a commercial install case with an inverter error. They start a swarm, Expert Finder invites an available inverter specialist, they work it out in the channel, and the agent uses Send to Salesforce to post the key Slack message onto the case. Then they click Finish Swarming and close the case. It needs the Slack integration and is set up through Salesforce Go. I'd agree with support leadership which case types qualify for a swarm, so experts aren't pulled in for everything.
points: Slack channel per case for expert collaboration
Begin Swarming and Finish Swarming actions
Expert Finder suggests available experts by skill
Send to Salesforce saves key messages on the case

q: How does Email-to-Case threading work now that Ref ID threading is being replaced?
alt: What is Lightning threading in Email-to-Case?
thread id vs thread token salesforce
how does salesforce match email replies to cases
Ref ID retirement email to case what to change
a: Email-to-Case now matches replies to cases using a token plus email header data, instead of the old ref ID string in the subject or body. When an agent emails from the case, Salesforce adds a thread token and the outgoing email carries header metadata. When the customer replies, Email-to-Case checks the token first, then the headers, and only creates a new case if neither matches. It's turned on through the release update that disables Ref ID and moves to the new threading behavior. Example: a hotel chain's email templates still use the old Case.Thread_Id merge field. Before enabling the update, I'd have the team switch templates to Case.Thread_Token, replace Cases.getCaseIdFromEmailThreadId in custom Apex with Cases.getCaseIdFromEmailHeaders or EmailMessages.getRecordIdFromEmail, and test real reply chains in a sandbox. I'd treat it as a planned change with a test checklist, because a threading break shows up straight away as duplicate cases.
points: Token first, then email headers, else new case
Enabled via the Ref ID release update
Templates: Case.Thread_Id becomes Case.Thread_Token
Apex: use getCaseIdFromEmailHeaders or getRecordIdFromEmail

q: Explain milestone actions and recurrence types in an entitlement process.
alt: What are success, warning and violation actions?
milestone recurrence independent vs sequential
How do milestone actions work in salesforce
Give an example of milestone criteria and actions
a: Each milestone can have three kinds of timed actions: warning actions fire before the target, violation actions fire when it's missed, and success actions fire when it's completed in time. Actions can send an email alert, update a field or create a task, and a field update can kick off a flow for anything more complex. Recurrence decides how often a milestone happens on one case: No Recurrence means once per case, Independent means a new milestone each time the criteria become true, and Sequential means it repeats, but each new one starts only after the previous one is completed. Example: a hospital IT desk wants a two-hour response on high-priority tickets. At 90 minutes the warning emails the owner and team lead, at 120 the violation reassigns the ticket to an urgent queue, and the success action marks the SLA as met. Something like 'respond to every customer email within four hours' fits Sequential. In design reviews I check that every violation action has a clear owner, otherwise the alert just becomes noise.
points: Warning, violation and success actions
Email alert, field update, task; field update can trigger a flow
Recurrence: No Recurrence, Independent, Sequential
Business hours drive the target time

q: What are business hours and holidays used for in Service Cloud?
alt: Why do we need business hours on cases?
business hours in escalation rules and milestones
how to exclude weekends from SLA
BusinessHours class in Apex
a: Business hours define when your support team works, and Salesforce uses them to calculate SLA and escalation times, so the clock doesn't run on a Sunday night. You create business hours records with a time zone and weekly hours, attach Holidays to them, and mark one as the default. Escalation rules, entitlement processes and milestones use them, and each case has a Business Hours field. Example: a bank has an India team working 9 to 6 IST. A case with a four-hour response target created at 5 p.m. gets a target late the next morning, and if a festival day is set as a holiday, the clock skips that day too. For custom logic, the BusinessHours class in Apex has methods like add, diff and isWithin, so you can calculate a due date the same way the platform does. On my teams the rule is to use that class instead of hand-rolled date maths.
points: Business hours have time zone and weekly schedule
Holidays attach to business hours
Used by escalation rules, entitlements, milestones

q: What are the main objects in the Service Cloud data model?
alt: Explain the Service Cloud data model
which standard objects does service cloud use
objects related to case in salesforce
What is AgentWork, MessagingSession and VoiceCall?
a: The center is Case, linked to Account, Contact and often Asset. Around it are EmailMessage for emails, CaseComment and feed items for the feed, CaseTeamMember for case teams, and CaseHistory for field tracking. For SLAs there's Entitlement, ServiceContract and ContractLineItem, plus CaseMilestone records created by the entitlement process. Knowledge articles live in Knowledge__kav, and CaseArticle links articles to cases. Channels add their own objects: MessagingSession and MessagingEndUser for chat and messaging, VoiceCall for Service Cloud Voice. Omni-Channel uses PendingServiceRouting while an item waits and AgentWork once it's offered to an agent. Example: for one broken washing machine you might see the case, two EmailMessages, a completed CaseMilestone, a CaseArticle and an AgentWork record that shows which agent took it and how long it took. I make sure new developers on the team know these, because it makes reports and SOQL much easier.

q: What are PendingServiceRouting and AgentWork, and how would you use them in Apex?
alt: How do you do skills-based routing from Apex?
pending service routing skill requirement example
What is AgentWork object used for?
route a case with skills using apex code
a: PendingServiceRouting is the record Omni-Channel uses while a work item is waiting to be routed, and AgentWork is created when it's offered to and taken by an agent. A common use is skills-based routing from Apex: you insert a PendingServiceRouting for each case with IsReadyForRouting false, add SkillRequirement records for, say, Spanish and Warranty, then set IsReadyForRouting to true so Omni-Channel starts looking for an agent. AgentWork is great for reporting and automation because it holds the user, the work item, and times like handle time and speed to answer. Example: a gadget company wants to alert a supervisor when a VIP case has waited ten minutes; a scheduled flow or job can query PendingServiceRouting for VIP cases older than that. My standard today is to try an Omni-Channel flow first and use Apex only when the logic is too complex for a flow, because flows are easier for the wider team to maintain.
points: PendingServiceRouting = waiting work; AgentWork = assigned work
