q: What are bulk macros and irreversible macros?
alt: Can macros run on multiple cases at once?
irreversible macro meaning salesforce
run a macro from a list view
What are the limitations of macros?
a: A macro is a saved set of steps an agent runs with one click, and bulk and irreversible macros are two special kinds. A bulk macro can run on many records at once from a list view, but only if its steps can run without the agent filling something in on screen, so macros that need the agent to edit text in the publisher can't be used in bulk. An irreversible macro has a step that can't be undone, like submitting an email or posting to the feed, so agents should check the record before running it. Example: during a shipping delay, a retailer's supervisor selects many 'where is my order' cases in a list view and runs a bulk macro that sets Status to Waiting on Carrier and posts a standard update. One thing I check before rolling out a macro: macros act on what's on the page, so the page layout and publisher actions must include the fields and actions the macro uses.
points: Bulk macros run from list views on many records
Not every macro can run in bulk
Irreversible macros contain steps like sending an email
Macros depend on the page layout and publisher actions

q: What would you put in the Service Console utility bar, and which console features help agents most?
alt: What is the utility bar in a console app?
service console features split view subtabs
How do you set up a Lightning Service Console for agents?
console navigation rules and workspace tabs
a: The utility bar is the strip at the bottom of a console app for tools agents need on every tab, so I put the Omni-Channel widget there, plus the softphone, History, Macros and maybe a notes component. Beyond that, the console helps with workspace tabs and subtabs, so a case opens with its contact and account as subtabs and the agent never loses context, and split view, which shows a list on the side while they work a record. Example: an airline agent goes online in Omni-Channel from the utility bar, a lost baggage case opens as a new tab with the contact as a subtab, and the agent runs a 'Baggage claim acknowledgement' macro from the utility bar. Navigation rules, like opening contacts as subtabs of cases, and keyboard shortcuts save more clicks. I also keep the case page focused, with the feed and Knowledge components where agents actually look. I'd validate that layout by sitting with a couple of agents, not just designing it in Setup.
points: Utility bar: Omni-Channel, softphone, History, Macros
Workspace tabs and subtabs keep context
Split view for working through lists
Navigation rules and keyboard shortcuts

q: High-priority cases must get a first response within 2 hours, counting only business hours. How would you build it?
alt: How do you implement a 2 hour SLA for high priority cases?
first response time SLA in salesforce
high priority case must be answered in two hours
set up response time commitment with milestones
a: I'd build it with an entitlement process and a First Response milestone, not custom date maths. Steps: create business hours for the support team and add holidays. Create an entitlement process using those hours, and add a First Response milestone with criteria Priority equals High and a 120-minute time trigger. Add a warning action at 90 minutes that emails the owner and team lead, a violation action that reassigns to an Urgent queue and alerts the manager, and a success action that ticks a 'Response SLA Met' field. Then make sure every case gets an entitlement, with a before-save flow that finds the account's active entitlement. Finally, complete the milestone automatically when the agent sends the first email, with a flow or trigger on EmailMessage. Example: at a payroll software company with 9 to 6 hours, a High case logged at 4:30 p.m. gets a target of 9:30 the next morning, not 6:30 that evening. I'd confirm the holiday calendar with the support manager before go-live.
points: Business hours plus entitlement process
Milestone criteria Priority = High, 120 minutes
Warning, violation and success actions
Auto-set entitlement and auto-complete milestone

q: Emails to support are creating duplicate cases. Write Apex to detect and link the duplicates.
alt: Apex trigger to prevent duplicate email to case cases
dedupe email to case with code
customer emails twice and two cases get created
How do you flag duplicate cases from email in a trigger?
a: I'd flag duplicates at insert instead of deleting them, so no email is ever lost. A before insert trigger on Case looks only at Email-to-Case cases, builds a key from the sender address and a cleaned subject without RE: or FW:, and queries open cases from the same sender in the last two days. If one matches, the new case gets ParentId set to the original and a closed status like Closed - Duplicate, so agents work only the original while the email is still visible on the linked child. Example: a furniture store customer emails 'Sofa not delivered' and ten minutes later 'RE: Sofa not delivered' from a different thread; the second case is linked and closed. Things I'd check in code review: Closed - Duplicate must exist as a closed status, auto-response rules may still fire, and two duplicates in the same batch need extra handling. Lightning threading should already stop real replies from creating new cases.
points: Key = sender email + normalized subject
Query recent open cases in bulk, one SOQL
Link with ParentId and close as duplicate, never delete
Fix the source and use Lightning threading too

q: Agents are getting overloaded with chats. What would you do?
alt: Too many concurrent chats per agent, how to fix
agents complain they get too many messaging sessions at once
How do you control how many chats an agent handles?
chat volume overwhelming support team
a: First I'd figure out whether it's a capacity setting problem or a real volume problem, because the fixes are very different. On the settings side, I check the presence configuration's capacity and the units of capacity each messaging item uses in the routing configuration. Example: if agents have capacity 10 and each chat uses 2, they get five chats at once, which is too many for complex warranty chats; making each chat weigh 4 limits them to two. I'd also give agents a status like 'Available - Cases Only' so they can step off chat for a while, and check whether auto-accept is on. If it's real volume, I'd put an Agentforce service agent in front to answer simple questions like order status, improve Knowledge for self-service, add overflow staffing at peak hours, and set customer expectations on wait time. Then I'd check the result in Omni Supervisor by watching concurrent chats per agent and wait times.
points: Check presence capacity and units of capacity per chat
Separate presence statuses for chat and cases
Deflect simple chats with an AI agent and Knowledge
Monitor in Omni Supervisor

q: Cases created on the Experience Cloud portal are not visible to the customer who created them. What would you check?
alt: Portal users cannot see their own cases
customer community user can not view case
cases missing from My Cases in experience site
Why can a customer not see a case in the portal?
a: My bet is a sharing problem or a missing contact link, so I check in this order. One: is the case's ContactId the customer's own contact? If the case is created by a flow in system context or by an integration user, the contact can end up blank, and then sharing never applies. Two: external sharing. With the external OWD on Case set to Private, customer community users need a sharing set giving access to cases where Contact matches their contact, or Account for account-wide access, while Customer Community Plus users rely on roles and sharing rules. Three: the profile or permission set needs Read on Case and access to the record type. Four: the list view or component on the site; 'My Cases' might filter by owner instead of contact. Example: a medical device company's portal form created cases owned by a queue with a blank contact, so customers saw nothing; setting ContactId from the logged-in user fixed it.
points: Check ContactId on the case first
Sharing sets for customer community users
Roles and sharing rules for Community Plus
Object, record type and list view filters

q: After moving from legacy Chat to Enhanced Chat, the support manager's chat reports are empty. What do you do?
alt: Live chat transcript reports not working after migration
how to report on enhanced chat
legacy chat reports to messaging session reports
Chat dashboards broke after Enhanced Chat migration
a: The reports are empty because Enhanced Chat uses a different data model, so old Live Chat Transcript reports won't get new data. Legacy Chat was retired in February 2026, so these need to be rebuilt, not patched. Steps: list every legacy report and dashboard and the metric each one shows. Then map them: conversation volume and status come from Messaging Session, response times and message counts come from the Messaging Session Metrics object, and handle time and speed to answer come from AgentWork. Create custom report types where needed, like Messaging Sessions with Cases, rebuild the dashboards, and keep the old transcript reports as a historical view. Example: a cosmetics retailer's dashboard showed chats per agent per day; now that's an AgentWork report filtered to the messaging channel and grouped by user and date. I'd also move any flows or triggers that ran on LiveChatTranscript over to MessagingSession. I'd walk the support manager through the new metrics, because some numbers will be defined differently from the old reports.
points: Enhanced Chat does not write LiveChatTranscript
Messaging Session, Messaging Session Metrics, AgentWork
Custom report types and rebuilt dashboards
Move automation to MessagingSession

q: The business wants to capture an order number before a chat starts and route the chat based on it. How would you do it?
alt: How do you set up pre-chat fields in Enhanced Chat?
pass pre chat data to omni channel flow
route chat based on pre-chat form values
hidden pre-chat fields messaging for web
a: I'd use Enhanced Chat pre-chat fields with an Omni-Channel flow. Steps: in the messaging channel, add custom parameters like OrderNumber and IssueType, and expose them on the pre-chat form in the embedded service deployment, visible fields for the customer and hidden fields the website fills, like whether they're logged in. Map the parameters to flow variables in the channel's parameter mappings. In the Omni-Channel flow, look up the order by number, find the account and its tier, and then set skills or pick a queue. Example: a mobile accessories store sends chats with issue type 'Damaged item' on high-value orders to the Returns team with a Priority skill, and everything else to an Agentforce service agent first. I'd also save the order number on the Messaging Session or the case, so the agent doesn't have to ask the customer again. I'd also agree with the web team who owns the hidden fields, since a website change can quietly break routing.
points: Custom parameters as visible or hidden pre-chat fields
Parameter mappings into the Omni-Channel flow
Look up order and account, then set skills or queue
Store the value so the agent sees it

q: How would you automatically classify and route thousands of emailed cases every day?
alt: Design email triage at high volume
auto categorize and route email cases
we get thousands of support emails, how to sort them
How would you reduce manual triage of cases?
a: I'd combine better intake, AI classification and data-driven routing. First, separate routing addresses where it makes sense, like billing@ and returns@, so the Origin and a category are set at the source. Second, turn on Einstein Case Classification trained on clean historical cases to predict Reason, Product and Priority, and auto-fill only the fields that prove accurate. Third, route with an Omni-Channel flow: read the predicted fields, add skills like product and language, raise routing priority for premium entitlements, and use fallback queues. Fourth, deflect: for simple requests like order status, an auto-response with relevant articles or an automated reply flow can resolve them without an agent. Example: an electronics marketplace getting several thousand emails a day can drop most of its manual triage team's work this way. I'd track misroutes with a reassignment count on the case and review rules and the model regularly. I'd also set expectations with the support director that accuracy improves over time, so we start with the safe fields.
points: Separate routing addresses for early categorization
Case Classification for Reason, Product, Priority
Omni-Channel flow with skills and priorities
Deflect simple requests; track misroutes

q: A high-priority customer's SLA is about to breach and the assigned agent is unavailable. How would you prevent the breach?
alt: How do you avoid SLA violation when owner is out
case about to miss milestone and agent is offline
reassign case automatically before SLA breach
Design SLA protection for VIP customers
a: I'd make the system notice early and move the work, rather than hope the agent comes back. Setup: the case has an entitlement with a milestone. A warning action at, say, 75 percent of the target updates an 'SLA at risk' field, and a record-triggered flow on that field checks whether the owner is online, using the UserServicePresence object, or marked out of office. If not, the flow sends the case back into a priority queue with high routing priority, or re-routes it by skills through Omni-Channel, and notifies the team lead by email or Slack. The violation action escalates to the manager. Example: a cloud hosting company's platinum customer has a server-down case with a one-hour target; at 45 minutes the owner is in a meeting, so the flow moves it to the on-call queue and the next available senior engineer gets it. Afterwards, a report on at-risk cases shows where staffing is thin. I'd agree the at-risk threshold with the support manager, so alerts come early enough to act on.
points: Warning action sets an at-risk flag early
Flow checks owner presence via UserServicePresence
Re-route with high priority and notify the lead
Violation escalates to management

q: An agent is out sick and their assigned cases are stuck. How would you handle it now and prevent it later?
alt: Cases stuck with an absent agent
agent on leave, how to reassign their cases
how to move cases back to queue in salesforce
What if the case owner is not available?
a: Right now I'd put the cases back into circulation. A supervisor opens a list view of open cases owned by that agent, sorts by priority, and changes the owner to the team queue, highest priority first; Omni-Channel then pushes them to whoever is available. Example: at a utility company an agent calls in sick with twelve open cases, three of them high priority; the team lead filters 'My Team's Open Cases' by owner and moves them all to the Billing queue in a couple of minutes. To prevent it, I'd keep fewer cases sitting with individuals by using Waiting statuses and status-based capacity, add milestone warnings that alert the lead when a case is idle too long, and give supervisors a simple screen flow like 'Return this agent's cases to queue'. Some teams also add an out-of-office flag on the user that routing checks before assigning. I'd write that up as a short runbook so any team lead can do it.
points: Reassign to the queue, highest priority first
Omni-Channel redistributes automatically
Milestone warnings catch idle cases
Supervisor flow and out-of-office flag

q: Unresolved cases should be escalated to the support manager after 8 business hours. How would you do it?
alt: How do you set up an escalation rule?
escalate case if not resolved in 8 hours
auto escalate old cases to manager
escalation rule with business hours example
a: I'd use an escalation rule; this is a classic job for one. Steps: make sure business hours exist for the team. In the escalation rule, add an entry with criteria like Status not equal to Closed, plus any priority or type filter, choose to use business hours, and decide how age is counted: from creation, from creation but stop after the case is first modified, or from the last modification. Add an escalation action with Age Over 8 hours that reassigns the case to the manager or an Escalations queue and sends a notification email. When it fires, the case's Escalated flag is set, so you can report on it. Example: a printer manufacturer with 9 to 6 hours gets a case at 2 p.m. Monday; if it's still open, it escalates at 1 p.m. Tuesday. The risk I'd flag to the manager: with 'based on last modified', agents who keep touching the case without solving it reset the clock. If entitlements are in use, a milestone violation action can do the same job.
points: Escalation rule entry with criteria and business hours
Choose how age is calculated
Action: Age Over 8 hours, reassign and notify
IsEscalated flag for reporting

q: A case should not be closed while it has open child cases or open tasks. How would you enforce it?
alt: Prevent closing parent case with open child cases
validation to block case close if open tasks exist
trigger to stop case closure
How do you stop agents closing a case with pending work?
a: A validation rule can't look at child records, so I'd use a before update trigger, or a record-triggered flow with a Custom Error element if the team prefers flows. The trigger collects cases moving into a closed status, runs one query for open child cases and one for open tasks, and adds an error to any case that still has open work. Example: an equipment rental company opens child cases for delivery, installation and billing under one parent; the agent tries to close the parent while billing is still open and gets 'Close all child cases and tasks first'. I check closed status values through the CaseStatus object rather than hard-coding names, so new closed statuses work automatically. Both queries are bulk-safe, so a data load closing thousands of cases still works. In review I'd also check the error message tells the agent what's still open.
points: Validation rules cannot see child records
Before update trigger with addError
Use CaseStatus to find closed values
Two bulk queries: child cases and tasks

q: A customer has three products with different support levels. How would you model their SLAs?
alt: Different SLA per product for the same account
service contracts and contract line items design
entitlement per asset or product
How do you handle multiple support plans for one customer?
a: I'd use a service contract for the agreement, a contract line item per product, and entitlements at the line item or asset level, so the SLA follows what the customer actually bought. Example: a hospital buys Platinum support for its MRI machine, Gold for ultrasound, and Standard for software. One service contract holds the deal, three contract line items point to the products or assets, and each gets an entitlement tied to a different entitlement process with its own milestones and business hours, like 24x7 for the MRI. When a case is logged against the MRI asset, a before-save flow finds the active entitlement on that asset or line item and sets it on the case, so the four-hour Platinum milestones start. Decisions I'd get agreed with the business: what happens when no entitlement matches, use start and end dates so expired entitlements are ignored, and use entitlement process versions when terms change.
points: Service contract + contract line items per product
Entitlements on line items or assets
Different entitlement processes and business hours
Flow picks the entitlement from the case asset

q: Agents keep typing the same answers again and again. How would you speed them up?
alt: Reduce repetitive typing for support agents
quick text vs macro vs knowledge for repeated replies
agents write same email many times
How can agents reply faster in the console?
a: I'd look at what they repeat and give them the right tool for each. For short phrases and greetings, Quick Text with merge fields, like 'Hi {!Contact.FirstName}, thanks for contacting us about {!Case.Subject}'. For repeated multi-step work, a macro, for example 'Request proof of purchase' that opens the email action, inserts a template, sets Status to Waiting on Customer and sends. For repeated technical answers, Knowledge articles that agents insert into replies, so the content is kept accurate in one place. On messaging channels, Reply Recommendations or Service Replies can suggest answers. Example: a camera shop's agents answer 'how do I reset my camera' many times a week; one article plus a macro turns that into two clicks. I'd measure handle time before and after so the team sees the difference. I'd also give one person ownership of the macro and template library, so it doesn't sprawl.
points: Quick Text for short reusable phrases
Macros for multi-step actions
Knowledge for technical answers
AI reply suggestions on messaging

q: Web-to-Case is creating lots of spam cases. How would you stop it?
alt: Spam cases from website form
how to add captcha to web to case
bots submitting web to case form
junk cases coming from the contact us page
a: I'd block the bots at the form first, then catch whatever gets through. Step one: turn on reCAPTCHA in the Web-to-Case settings and regenerate the form HTML on the website, because the old form code won't include it. Step two: if spam continues, move the form to an Experience Cloud page or a screen flow, which gives better validation and control. Step three: inside Salesforce, add a before-save flow that marks obvious spam, like known junk domains or links in the description, and an assignment rule entry at the top that sends those cases to a Spam queue so agents never see them. Example: a furniture store's contact form gets hundreds of junk cases overnight with crypto links; reCAPTCHA stops most, and the rule parks the rest. The risk I'd point out to the business: Web-to-Case has a daily limit, so heavy spam can actually block real customers once it's hit.
points: Enable reCAPTCHA and regenerate the form
Consider an Experience Cloud or flow-based form
Flag spam and route to a Spam queue
Daily Web-to-Case limit can be eaten by spam

q: Auto-response emails should be different for each brand and language. How would you set it up?
alt: Multiple auto response templates by language
auto response rule entries for different brands
send acknowledgement email in customer language
How do auto-response rule entries work?
a: I'd do it with auto-response rule entries, because only one case auto-response rule can be active, but it can have many entries checked in order. Steps: create email templates per brand and language, like 'Brand A - English' and 'Brand A - Spanish'. In the auto-response rule, add entries with criteria on a Brand field and a Language field, set from the web form, the routing address or the contact, and pick the matching template plus the sender name and email address. The first matching entry wins, so I order them from specific to general and put a default entry at the end. Example: a cosmetics group with two brands gets a case for Brand B from a French-speaking contact; the entry 'Brand = B and Language = French' sends the French Brand B template from the Brand B support address. When testing in a sandbox, check that email deliverability is set to All email. I'd keep that entry order documented, because whoever adds the next brand needs to know where it goes.
points: One active auto-response rule, many ordered entries
First match wins; default entry last
Templates per brand and language
Set sender name and address per entry

q: A complex enterprise case needs the account manager, a sales engineer and a support engineer working on it together. How would you set it up?
alt: How do you give multiple people access to one case?
case team roles example
predefined case teams use case
collaborate on a case without changing owner
a: I'd use Case Teams, so the right people get access and are visible on the case without changing the owner. Steps: create Case Team Roles like Account Manager with Read Only access and Sales Engineer and Support Engineer with Read/Write. Optionally create a predefined case team, say 'Enterprise Escalation', with the usual members. Add the Case Team related list to the case page, and use a flow to add the predefined team automatically when a case on a strategic account gets escalated. Example: a networking company's biggest customer reports a data center outage; the support engineer stays the owner, and the account manager and sales engineer are added as team members, so they can see updates and follow the feed. For real-time discussion on top of that, I'd start a swarm in Slack. Case team membership also lets you build reports like 'cases I'm on' for people who aren't the owner. I'd agree the team roles with support leadership up front, so access is consistent across escalations.
points: Case Team Roles define access level
Predefined case teams for common groups
Flow can add the team automatically
Combine with Slack swarming for live discussion

q: A case needs an on-site technician. How would you hand it off to Field Service?
alt: Case to work order handoff
how does service cloud connect to field service
create work order from case for technician visit
Field Service integration with cases
a: My design rule here is that the case stays the customer's main record, and the field work hangs off it through a Work Order. Steps: the agent troubleshoots first; if a visit is needed, they use a 'Create Work Order' quick action on the case that copies the account, contact, asset, address and the right Work Type, like 'Boiler Repair - 2 hours'. The work type can create the Service Appointment automatically with duration and required skills. The dispatcher or the scheduling optimizer books a technician, who works the job in the Field Service mobile app. When the job is done, a flow updates the case, say to Pending Confirmation, and adds the technician's notes, so the agent can confirm with the customer and close. Example: a heating company's customer has no hot water, the phone fix fails, the agent creates a work order, and when the customer calls back, the case shows the visit time. If SLAs apply on site, carry the entitlement onto the work order too.
points: Quick action creates Work Order from Case
Work Type can auto-create the Service Appointment
Technician completes in the mobile app
Flow updates the case when the job finishes

q: Tier 2 engineers don't work in Salesforce; they live in Slack. How would you get their help on cases?
alt: Engineers use Slack not Salesforce, how to collaborate on cases
bring slack experts into a case
use slack for case escalation
How would you set up swarming for a support team?
a: I'd bring the case to them in Slack with Swarming instead of forcing them into the console. Steps: set up the Slack integration and swarming through Salesforce Go, make Begin Swarming available on the case, and set up skills so Expert Finder can suggest the right engineers. Example: a SaaS company's agent has a case where data exports fail for one customer. They click Begin Swarming, a channel named after the case number is created, they describe the problem, and two backend engineers join. The engineers discuss in Slack, one finds the bug, and the agent uses Send to Salesforce to put the answer on the case, then clicks Finish Swarming and closes it. The case keeps the knowledge and the engineers stay in the tool they already use. I'd agree on ground rules like keeping customer data in private swarm channels and using Slack Connect only with admin approval for external people. Those ground rules are what I'd get signed off by security before rollout.
points: Swarming set up through Salesforce Go
Channel per case, experts via Expert Finder
Send to Salesforce keeps the answer on the case
Rules for private channels and external users

q: Spanish-speaking customers should reach Spanish-speaking agents. How would you set it up?
alt: Language based routing in Omni-Channel
route chats by customer language
skills based routing for language example
How do you match customers with agents who speak their language?
a: I'd use Omni-Channel skills-based routing with a language skill. Steps: create skills like Spanish and English and give them to agents as service resource skills. Capture the customer's language at intake: a pre-chat field in Enhanced Chat, a separate routing address for email like soporte@, or the language on the contact. Then an Omni-Channel flow or skills-based routing rule adds the matching skill requirement. Set a fallback: mark the language as an additional skill that can be dropped after a timeout, or send the item to a general queue, so customers don't wait forever. Example: a travel agency in Miami gets a WhatsApp message in Spanish; the flow adds Spanish and Booking skills, and it goes only to bilingual booking agents who are online. I'd watch wait time by language in Omni Supervisor to see if more Spanish-speaking agents are needed. The fallback timeout is a business decision, so I'd agree it with the support manager rather than guess.
points: Language skills on service resources
Capture language from pre-chat, address or contact
Omni-Channel flow adds skill requirements
Fallback by dropping skills after a timeout

q: Omni-Channel pushes work, but agents ignore or decline it and items keep bouncing around. What would you check?
alt: Work items bounce between agents in Omni-Channel
agents declining omni channel requests
push timeout omni channel problem
Cases keep getting re-routed to different agents
a: I'd look at the push settings, the routing rules and the reasons agents give. In the routing configuration, check the push timeout: if it's short, items that agents miss bounce to the next agent and back. In the presence configuration, check whether agents are allowed to decline and whether they must pick a decline reason, then report on declined work to see why. Consider auto-accept, which stops agents from skipping items they don't like. In the routing configuration and skills, check whether the item needs a skill only one or two agents have, because then it keeps cycling between them. Example: at a pharmacy chain, agents declined refill-delay cases because those needed calls to suppliers; the fix was a separate skill and queue for those cases plus some coaching. Omni Supervisor helps here too, since it shows which agents have work waiting and how long items sit in the queue. I'd also talk to the agents, because declines usually point to a routing design problem, not just behaviour.
points: Push timeout too short causes bouncing
Decline settings and decline reasons
Auto-accept to stop cherry-picking
Rare skills make items cycle

q: The support director wants to measure average handle time, speed to answer and first contact resolution. How would you do it?
alt: How do you report on handle time in Service Cloud?
support KPIs in salesforce reports
measure first contact resolution
AgentWork reporting for speed to answer
a: I'd use AgentWork for time metrics and the case itself for resolution metrics. AgentWork, created by Omni-Channel, stores when work was assigned, accepted and closed, plus handle time and speed to answer, so a report on AgentWork grouped by agent and channel gives average handle time and speed to answer. For first contact resolution there's no standard field, so I'd add a checkbox on Case set by a flow when a case closes with only one inbound contact and no reopen, or let agents tick it on close for phone. A reopen count, increased by a flow whenever a closed case reopens, helps too. Example: a broadband provider builds a dashboard with handle time per queue, speed to answer by hour of day, and FCR per team, and uses it to plan shifts. For messaging, the Messaging Session Metrics object adds response times and message counts. Before building, I'd agree the FCR definition with the director, because every team defines it a bit differently.
points: AgentWork: handle time and speed to answer
FCR needs a custom field set by flow
Reopen count as a quality signal
Messaging Session Metrics for chat

q: Agents need to see the customer's orders from the ERP on the case without leaving the console. How would you build it?
alt: Show external system data on a case
display SAP orders in service console
salesforce connect vs lwc callout for agents
How do you give agents a 360 view of the customer?
a: I'd decide between showing the data live and copying it in, based on how fresh it must be and whether it's needed in reports. For live, read-only data, Salesforce Connect with external objects, or an LWC that calls the ERP through Apex and a named credential, shows the orders as a related list or component on the case. If agents need to report on orders or use them in automation, I'd sync a slim order object on a schedule or through events instead. Example: a spare parts distributor's agent opens a case and sees the last five orders with shipping status, pulled live from the ERP, with a button to open the full order. Points to discuss: callout timeouts and friendly error messages in the component, caching for speed, and field-level access so agents only see what they should. The same Apex action can later be reused by an Agentforce agent for 'where is my order'. I'd put that live-versus-copy decision in front of the business with the trade-offs, since it drives cost and maintenance.
points: Live: Salesforce Connect or LWC with named credential
Copy: scheduled or event-based sync for reporting
Handle timeouts and errors in the UI
Reuse the action for an AI agent

q: Holiday shutdowns and time spent waiting on the customer should not count against the SLA. How would you handle it?
alt: Pause SLA clock while waiting on customer
stop milestone timer salesforce
exclude holidays from SLA calculation
How do you pause entitlements on a case?
a: I'd use two separate tools: business hours with holidays for shutdowns, and stopping milestones for waiting time. For holidays, add Holiday records to the support business hours and make sure the entitlement process and cases use those hours, so target dates skip those days automatically. For waiting time, the case has a Stopped checkbox; while it's true, milestones pause, and their targets move out by the stopped time when it's cleared. I'd set it with a flow: when Status changes to Waiting on Customer, set Stopped to true, and when the customer replies and the case goes back to In Progress, set it to false. Example: an accounting software vendor closes for a year-end week and often asks customers for log files; without this, many cases would show violations that weren't the team's fault. I'd add a report on stopped time so the pause isn't misused.
points: Holidays on business hours skip shutdown days
Case Stopped checkbox pauses milestones
Flow sets and clears Stopped by status
Report on stopped time

q: A customer starts a chat while they already have an open case about the same issue. How do you keep it together?
alt: Link messaging session to existing case
avoid new case when customer chats about open issue
connect chat with existing case salesforce
How do you route a chat to the agent who owns the open case?
a: I'd link the conversation to the existing case instead of creating a new one. In the Omni-Channel flow, or a small flow on the Messaging Session, look up open cases for the messaging end user's contact. If there's exactly one recent open case, set the Messaging Session's case lookup to it and try to route to that case owner if they're online. If there are several, let the agent pick from the contact's open cases in the console. Example: a phone repair shop's customer emailed yesterday about a delayed repair and now opens a chat; the flow finds the open case, attaches the chat to it, and the same agent gets the conversation. When the chat ends, the transcript stays on the Messaging Session related to the case, so the case history is complete. I'd agree with the business on when a new issue deserves its own case. That rule is what I'd document for the team, so agents handle it the same way.
points: Find open cases for the messaging end user contact
Set the case lookup on the Messaging Session
Route to the case owner with a fallback
Agent chooses when there are several

q: Customers want to reach the same agent who helped them last time. How would you set it up?
alt: Preferred agent routing in Omni-Channel
route to last agent who handled the customer
agent affinity routing salesforce
How do you route to a specific agent with fallback?
a: I'd route to a preferred agent with a fallback, using an Omni-Channel flow. Steps: in the flow, find the agent for this customer, for example the owner of the contact's most recent closed case, the last AgentWork user, or a Preferred Agent lookup on the account, which is easier for the business to control. Use the Route Work action to target that agent, and if they're offline or busy, fall back to the normal queue or skills routing. Example: a wealth management firm wants clients to reach their usual service rep; a client's chat goes to their rep first, and if the rep is in a meeting it goes to the team queue. The trade-off is continuity versus wait time, so I'd keep the fallback quick for urgent issues and report on how often the preferred agent actually handles the work. I'd agree the fallback time with the business up front, because it's a service decision, not a technical one.
points: Find preferred agent from history or account lookup
Route Work to the agent with fallback
Keep fallback short for urgent work
Report on preferred-agent hit rate

q: How would you set up Service Cloud for a company with three brands, each with its own support email and look?
alt: Multi-brand service cloud design
one org many brands email to case
different branding for support emails per brand
How do you handle multiple brands in a support org?
a: I'd keep one Case process where possible and split only the customer-facing parts by brand. Steps: add a Brand field on Case, set from the web form or site, or by a flow that reads the To address on the first incoming email. Each brand gets its own Email-to-Case routing address, org-wide email address, email templates with its own letterhead, and auto-response entries. Routing uses brand as a skill, or separate queues if the teams are different. Knowledge uses data categories for brand, and each brand gets its own Experience Cloud site with its own branding. Example: a hotel group with luxury, business and budget brands shares one agent pool, but replies to budget guests always come from the budget brand's support address with its logo. Reports and dashboards filter by brand. I'd avoid three record types unless the processes really differ, because that triples maintenance. That's the trade-off I'd explain to stakeholders: shared process, separate branding.
points: Brand field set at intake
Per-brand routing address, org-wide address, templates
Brand as a skill or separate queues
Data categories and a site per brand

q: Support has teams in India and the US and wants follow-the-sun coverage. How would you design routing and SLAs?
alt: Follow the sun support model in Salesforce
24x7 support with teams in different time zones
route cases to the region that is working
business hours for multiple support regions
a: I'd model each team's hours explicitly and let routing move work to whoever is working. Steps: create business hours for India and for the US, plus a 24x7 set if premium customers get round-the-clock SLAs. Each region has its own queue and presence configuration, and the Omni-Channel flow sends new work to the region that's open, using a small Apex action with BusinessHours.isWithin, or simply routes on a global skill so any online agent with it gets the item. For cases that need continuity, agents set a handover status with notes at shift end, and the next region picks them up. Entitlement processes use the 24x7 hours for premium customers and regional hours for standard ones. Example: a SaaS vendor's urgent case logged at 7 p.m. IST goes to the US morning team instead of waiting overnight. I'd watch gaps in Omni Supervisor and a report of cases with no activity across a shift change. I'd agree the handover standard with both team leads, because follow-the-sun fails at the handover, not in the config.
points: Business hours per region plus 24x7 for premium
Route to the open region or by global skill
Handover status and notes at shift end
Monitor gaps across shift changes

q: Agents in one region must not see cases from other regions. How would you design case security?
alt: Restrict case visibility by region
case sharing model design for support teams
data residency for cases in salesforce
How do you secure cases between support teams?
a: I'd set the Case org-wide default to Private and open access back up by region with roles and sharing rules, instead of giving people View All. Steps: a role hierarchy by region, like Support EMEA and Support APAC with managers above them; queues per region, since queue members can see cases the queue owns; and criteria-based sharing rules, for example cases where Region equals EMEA are shared with the EMEA support role. For cross-region escalations, case teams give temporary, explicit access. Make sure Omni-Channel only routes a region's work to that region's agents through queues or skills, because the agent who accepts a case becomes its owner and gets access. Example: a bank's German team must not see Indian customers' cases for data residency reasons. I'd apply the same thinking to reports and Knowledge, and test with a user from each region before go-live. I'd also get the data residency requirement in writing from compliance, so the design is checked against the actual rule.
points: Private OWD on Case
Regional roles, queues and criteria-based sharing
Case teams for cross-region escalation
Routing must respect the regional split

q: A service outage makes hundreds of customers contact support at once. How would you handle it in Service Cloud?
alt: Mass incident handling in service cloud
hundreds of cases about the same outage
parent case for outage and close all children
How do you manage a major incident in support?
a: I'd treat it as one problem with many affected customers, not hundreds of separate investigations, and I'd have this playbook ready before the outage happens. Steps: create a master record, either a parent case or an Incident record if Incident Management is set up, and link every related case to it, using a macro or a flow that matches keywords like 'login error' during the outage window. Post the known issue on the help portal and give the Agentforce service agent an answer for it so chat volume drops. Agents use a macro that links the case, sends a standard 'we're aware and working on it' reply and sets the status to Waiting on Fix. When the fix lands, a flow updates and closes all linked cases with a resolution email. Example: a payments app goes down for an hour, hundreds of cases arrive, and support handles them in a few bulk updates instead of one by one. Afterwards, the incident's linked cases feed the post-mortem.
points: One parent case or Incident record
Link cases by macro or keyword flow
Proactive portal banner and AI agent answer
Bulk close children when fixed

q: Cases created by Apex or an integration are not following assignment rules. Why, and how do you fix it?
alt: Assignment rules not firing for cases inserted via apex
DMLOptions assignmentRuleHeader example
integration user owns all cases
How do you run case assignment rules from code?
a: The cause is almost always the same: assignment rules don't run automatically when you insert cases from Apex, so the case stays with the running user or integration user. The fix is to set DML options with the assignment rule header before inserting, which tells Salesforce to apply the active rule, and you can request the auto-response email the same way. The standard REST API is different: it applies the active rule by default, and the Sforce-Auto-Assign header turns that off or names a rule. Example: a smart-home company's device platform creates cases through a custom Apex REST service when a thermostat reports a fault; they were all owned by the integration user until we added DML options, and now they land in the Devices queue. If you need a specific rule instead of the active one, set assignmentRuleId instead of useDefaultRule. Also check that no trigger or flow overwrites the owner afterwards. On my teams that DML options check is part of code review for any Apex that inserts cases.
points: Apex inserts skip assignment rules by default
Database.DMLOptions with assignmentRuleHeader
emailHeader for auto-response
REST applies the active rule by default; Sforce-Auto-Assign controls it

q: Email-to-Case suddenly stopped creating cases. How would you troubleshoot it?
alt: Emails not converting to cases
email to case not working anymore
support emails are not reaching salesforce
Why are no cases being created from email?
a: I'd follow the email's path from the customer's mailbox into Salesforce. One: is forwarding still working? Check that the company mailbox, like support@, still forwards to the Salesforce Email Services address; a mail server change or a removed forwarding rule is the most common cause. Two: is the routing address still set up and verified in the Email-to-Case settings? Three: is mail bouncing? Look for bounce or error messages in the support mailbox. Four: are cases failing on save, for example because of a new validation rule, a required field, or an error in a trigger or flow on Case or EmailMessage? These usually show up as error emails or in debug logs for the automated process. Five: check recent changes, like a deactivated user set as the case owner on the routing address. Example: at a logistics company, IT moved support@ to a new mail system and dropped the forwarding rule, so nothing reached Salesforce. Afterwards I'd ask IT to tell us before mail changes and add a simple alert if no cases arrive for a few hours.
points: Check mailbox forwarding first
Routing address set up and verified
Look for bounces and error emails
Validation rules or automation failing on save

q: The business wants agents to follow a guided troubleshooting script for certain case types. How would you do it?
alt: Guided scripts for support agents
screen flow on case record page for troubleshooting
step by step agent guidance in console
How do you make new agents follow the same process?
a: I'd build the script as a screen flow and show it on the case only for the right case types. Steps: design the flow with screens that ask questions, branch on the answers, and update the case at the end, like setting Root Cause and the next status. Put it on the case page in the Actions & Recommendations component or as a quick action, with component visibility so it only shows for Type equals Connectivity. Embed Knowledge where a step needs details. Example: an internet provider's script asks 'Are the router lights on?' and 'Have you restarted it?', then runs a line test through an Apex action; if everything fails, it creates a work order for a technician. New agents follow the same steps as experts, and you get data on where cases usually get stuck. For a lighter option, Agentforce Service Assistant can draft a resolution plan from the case details. I'd have senior agents review the script before launch, since they know where the real cases go off track.
points: Screen flow with branching questions
Show by case type with component visibility
Apex actions for tests and lookups
Flow data shows where cases get stuck

q: Replies to customers should come from the support address, not the agent's personal email. How would you set it up?
alt: Send case emails from support address
org wide email address for case replies
customer replies going to agent personal inbox
How do you set the From address on the case email action?
a: I'd set up an org-wide email address and make it the default From on the case email action. Steps: create and verify an org-wide address like support@ and allow the support profiles to use it. On the case Email quick action, set a predefined value for the From address so agents don't pick their own. With Email-to-Case, the routing address itself can be used as the From too. Add a Lightning email template or letterhead with the support signature. Example: a furniture retailer's agents replied from their own user email addresses, so customer replies went to personal inboxes and never reached the case. After switching the From to support@, every reply comes back through Email-to-Case and threads onto the right case. I'd also check deliverability and email authentication like SPF and DKIM, so emails sent from Salesforce for support@ don't land in spam. That's a setup I'd put on every support go-live checklist.
points: Org-wide email address, verified and allowed for profiles
Predefined From on the Email action
Templates or letterhead with team signature
Set up SPF and DKIM for deliverability

q: You are migrating historical cases with their emails from another help desk tool into Service Cloud. How would you plan it?
alt: Case data migration plan
migrate tickets and emails into salesforce
load old cases without triggering automation
How do you keep original created dates when migrating cases?
a: I'd load in dependency order and keep automation from firing on old data. Order: accounts, contacts, then cases, then EmailMessages and comments, then files as ContentVersion linked to cases. Store the old ticket ID in an external ID field on Case, so reruns can upsert instead of creating duplicates. Turn on the permission to set audit fields on record creation, so created dates keep their original values, and load closed cases with their real closed status. Before loading, switch off or bypass assignment rules, auto-response rules, escalation rules, entitlement processes, flows and triggers, using a bypass custom permission or setting, so thousands of old cases don't email customers. Example: a fitness equipment company moving three years of tickets runs it first in a full sandbox, checks a sample of cases with their email threads, then loads production over a weekend. Set the EmailMessage incoming flag correctly so the feed reads in the right direction. I'd get the business to sign off on the sample check before the production load.
points: Load order: accounts, contacts, cases, emails, files
External ID on Case for upserts
Set Audit Fields to keep original dates
Bypass rules, flows and triggers during load

q: How would you design an end-to-end Service Cloud implementation for an electronics retailer?
alt: Design a complete service cloud solution
service cloud implementation approach from scratch
how would you architect support in salesforce for a retailer
Walk me through a Service Cloud solution design
a: I'd design it around the customer journey: intake, routing, SLA, resolution and feedback, and keep it simple to run. Intake: Email-to-Case with Lightning threading, an Experience Cloud help center with Knowledge search, and Enhanced Chat with an Agentforce service agent for order status and returns. Routing: Omni-Channel flows with product and language skills, higher priority for VIPs, status-based capacity for cases and capacity weights for chat. SLA: entitlement processes for standard and extended-warranty customers, with milestones and warning actions. Resolution: a Service Console with macros, quick text, Knowledge, Case Classification and Service Replies, swarming for hard cases, and a work order handoff for in-home repairs. Feedback: a CSAT survey on close and dashboards on handle time, SLA compliance and deflection. Example: a customer chats about a TV that won't turn on; the AI agent checks the warranty and hands off to a TV specialist, who books a repair. I'd launch email and chat first, then voice. Phasing it that way keeps the risk manageable and lets the team learn from the first launch.
points: Intake: email, help center, Enhanced Chat with AI agent
Routing: Omni-Channel flows, skills, capacity
SLA: entitlements and milestones
Resolution tools, Field Service handoff, CSAT

q: Agents cherry-pick easy cases from the queue and leave the hard ones. How would you stop it?
alt: Agents picking easy cases from queue
stop cherry picking in support queue
move from queue list views to push routing
Why use Omni-Channel instead of queue list views?
a: I'd move from pull to push with Omni-Channel, so the system decides who gets the next case. Steps: connect the queues to a routing configuration with sensible routing priority, so urgent queues go first and, within the same priority, older items go before newer ones. Give agents a presence configuration with the right capacity, and optionally turn on auto-accept so they can't skip work. Then remove or limit the queue list views agents used for picking, and leave the full view to supervisors. Example: an insurance helpdesk saw simple address-change cases closed within an hour while claim disputes sat for days; once Omni-Channel pushed cases in order, the old disputes started moving. I'd use Omni Supervisor to watch backlog by queue and explain the change to the team first, because some agents feel push routing takes away control. Being upfront about why we're doing it usually takes care of most of the pushback.
points: Push routing with Omni-Channel
Routing priority, then oldest first
Auto-accept and limited queue list views
Monitor backlog in Omni Supervisor
